title: the infra profile has no field for a sender's second DKIM key, a zone's wildcard A or TXT, or DMARC sp=, and a key it has no field for parses and is never read -- MailerSend's ms1 and ms2 can only be under-declared
body:
FOUND at Prodinfra, in two parts. Filed into 0.1.8 on hv's ruling of 2026-09-24: "Yes, all in 0.1.8, please."
- THE SECOND DKIM KEY, 2026-09-08. MailerSend replaced one 1024-bit DKIM CNAME, mlsend2._domainkey, with two 2048-bit CNAMEs, ms1._domainkey and ms2._domainkey, and it rotates between them without the operator doing anything. That is vendor-stated, in a notice to account holders that day, and the app's banner corroborates it. laksa.io was migrated the same day, with mlsend2 left in place until the new pair verified. Prodinfra recorded this in its TN0001 (docs/notes/tn0001-estate-target-state.md, the section "The pair is no longer always a PAIR", and provenance row V5) at Prodinfra a0facea, and routed it to devbin-vc. It never arrived. devbin's history holds no trace of it: `git log -S` over every ref finds nothing for ms1 or for "two dkim". vc found the record on 2026-09-24 by searching Prodinfra's tree.
- sp= AND WILDCARDS, 2026-09-24. prodinfra-cc sent these to vc between their clock's 16:24Z and 16:31Z (vc's date -u read 16:32:16Z), together with the authority read that is 0142.

WHAT THE SCHEMA HOLDS, read at fe51e3c:
- A sender's DKIM is one record. lib/infra.check:221-223 reads senders.<name>.dkim.{name,type,value} as scalars, and infra_sender_pair_complete (lib/infra:201) asks for dkim.name. So a sender that publishes two keys can be declared only by dropping one, which makes a half pair by construction. The matched-pair invariant (lib/infra:176-190) exists to catch exactly that. TN0001 states the rule's arithmetic: a domain never holds an SPF include without every DKIM record that authorises it, and one record per sender was an assumption about vendors.
- DMARC is p= and rua=. _ic_dmarc_fields (lib/infra.check:262) reads those two tags from the live record and nothing else, so sp=, the policy for subdomains, has no field.
- A zone's wildcard records have no field. check asks nothing of `*.<fqdn>`.
- A key the schema has no field for is not refused. infra_validate_profile (lib/infra:231) checks names, uniqueness and senders, and never lists the keys it knows. So a profile that writes the missing fields parses, validates, and is never read.

DRIVEN by vc on 2026-09-24 at fe51e3c in a scratch clone, with the infra arms' fake dig logging every query:
- ONE PROFILE, THREE SILENT GAPS. The profile declared `dmarc.sp: reject` where the live record carries sp=none. It declared MailerSend's pair with ms1 alone where the live zone has no ms2. And it declared `wildcard.txt: "v=spf1 -all"` where the zone has no wildcard. Result: "4 assertion(s) held, 0 drift, 0 NOT MEASURED", rc 0. The run made five queries (NS, MX, TXT, ms1's CNAME, _dmarc's TXT). It asked nothing about ms2 or `*.alpha.example`, and it compared nothing but p= and rua= in the _dmarc record it read.
- BOTH KEYS AS A LIST. With senders.mailersend.dkim written as a sequence of two records, lib/config refuses: "sequences of maps are not supported", rc 1. So the fix needs a shape lib/config can parse, or lib/config learns sequences of maps. The build decides which, and says which in its resolution.

WHERE THE ESTATE KEEPS THEM TODAY, in Prodinfra's profiles, as `manual:` prose that check prints under "not machine-checkable" and never verifies:
- geodica.com: `dmarc_sp` (sp=reject, published 2026-09-23 with p=quarantine) and `wildcard_txt` (`*.geodica.com TXT "v=spf1 -all"`, published 2026-09-23 beside the wildcard A), at profiles/geodica/infra.yaml:63-65.
- playprolix.com: its `web` entry records that it has had no wildcard A or AAAA since hv deleted them on 2026-09-24, at profiles/geodica/infra.yaml:119-120. Its case is a declared ABSENCE.
- MailerSend is declared with mlsend2 alone in both profiles (profiles/geodica/infra.yaml:44-54 and profiles/matthewsinclair/infra.yaml:24-33), and geodica's comment says laksa.io also carries ms1 and ms2, "which it cannot hold".

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
- A sender may declare more than one DKIM record, and the matched-pair check asks for each one on the authoritative server and names each one that is missing. The one-record form keeps its meaning, so no profile in the fleet changes by upgrading.
- DMARC gains sp=, checked against the live record as p= is. When sp= is absent from the record, it inherits p=, and check says which value it compared.
- A domain may declare its wildcard A and TXT, each checked at `*.<fqdn>` on the authoritative server. A declared absence can be checked too, which is playprolix.com's case.
- Whether an unknown key is refused is decided at the build, since it is the mechanism that hid all three gaps. If it is refused, measure the fleet's profiles first, as 0133 measured every log: key. The decision goes into the resolution.
- lib/infra.reference.yaml documents each new field, and lib/pages/infra.md says what check reads.
- Arms for each field against the fake dig, red first at fe51e3c, with mutants. The reference profile parses. The drive is Prodinfra's two profiles against the live zones. Retiring each `manual:` entry this replaces is Prodinfra's own change, after devbin ships.

vc's. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling.

## Resolution

Fixed at 077661a. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED, on vc's rulings (decision 44). A sender's DKIM is declared in a labelled form under `dkim:`, told apart from the one-record form by whether `dkim` carries a field directly; each record is read by its declared type and judged alone, so a missing ms2 is a HALF PAIR naming ms2, and a failed read is NOT MEASURED for that record. `dmarc.sp`, inherited per leaf, is compared with the live sp= or with p= when there is none, a weak sp= is the `dmarc.sp.enforce` blind spot, and an sp with no policy in force is refused at parse. The p= guard is fixed: a declared policy against a record with no p= is drift. Wildcards `a`, `aaaa` and `txt` under a zone, each one value or `none`, are read at `*.<fqdn>` on the authoritative server, an absence is verified, and a CNAME there contradicts any `none`. A declared value is compared with the whole sorted set of records at its name, never a substring of the first one listed. An unknown key is refused at parse, before any nameserver is asked, from one table in lib/infra, _INFRA_PROFILE_KEYS; lib/config refuses a key nested under a key with a value, and a sequence under a sequence item. The SPF drift a failed DKIM read used to hide, and a TXT DKIM record compared raw, are fixed. init measures sp= and records one that differs under `unreviewed:`. DRIVEN over a recorded snapshot of the live zones: Prodinfra's three profiles print byte-identical output before and after, so no fleet profile changes on upgrade; vc's three-gap profile of fe51e3c, which read 4 held and 0 drift at rc 0, now reads all three gaps.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. `_IC_SENDER_SPF` is deleted and the header that claimed a cross-domain SPF comparison corrected; the comparison itself is not built and is on vc's parked list. `senders.*.dkim.type` has no allowed-word check, so a lower-case cname reads as a HALF PAIR; that predates 0143 and is on the parked list too. init measures neither wildcards nor DKIM, and the page says so.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell reviewed the code and the arms over three passes, each point built or answered; its review also found the sequence-under-an-item gap in lib/config, fixed here. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v3 on the rulings built as ruled, the drives and the evidence below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. On the 0142 base's lib, 42 of the 46 new arms red, each for its own reason -- exactly the new arms but the four controls meant to hold on both (the one-record form, the apex, init's equal sp=, the fleet's key shapes); the TXT-as-written arm red there in its wildcard half, and in its DKIM half against the mutant it guards, M45; and the fake's new refusal red against 0142's fake. 49 mutants, each against the arms it aims at: 48 killed. M46, a failed declared side taken as drift, survives as declared: reaching it needs a fault injected into sort or awk, and the branch it guards reports an error, never drift.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the nine 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on b10dd41 (0139, 0128, 0133, 0130, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0146, 0147), on a clean checkout (head 308cf21), 2026-09-25 11:34:20Z to 12:09:20Z: 1907 of 1907 ok, 0 not ok, no gaps, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree outside intent/.
